name: Chicken Tikka Masala
cuisine: British-Indian / North Indian restaurant-style (Punjabi tikka in a spiced onion-tomato masala)

ingredients.name: Mustard oil (sarson ka tel) or vegetable oil
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 tsp (half in marinade, half for brushing/charring)

ingredients.name: Onion (for tikka, petals)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ small onion, separated into petals

ingredients.name: Tomato
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1½ medium ripe, finely chopped or grated

equipment: Mixing bowl for marinating, with a lid or cling film
Something to char the tikka (a tandoor is not needed)
Skewers (metal, or bamboo soaked in water for 20 min)
Kadai or heavy-bottomed pan (about 20 cm) for the masala
Box grater for the tomato (optional; finely chopping works)
Chopping board and knife; spatula; tongs or a fork
Measuring spoons (or a regular teaspoon: 1 level tsp ≈ 5 ml)

steps.title: Cut the chicken
steps.text: Cut 150 g boneless chicken thigh into 6–8 chunks of 3–4 cm. Trim off large fat pieces.
steps.tip: wash your hands, knife and board with soap straight after handling raw chicken.
steps.visualCue: even chunks about the size of a large grape or small plum, a little bigger than for butter chicken
steps.videoShot: knife cutting thigh into chunky cubes
steps.watchOut: tiny or uneven pieces, which dry out and burn before the big ones char; recut the small ones and cook them last.

steps.title: First marinade
steps.text: In a bowl, mix the chicken with 1 tsp lemon juice, ¼ tsp salt and ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder.
steps.visualCue: every piece is tinted red with no dry white patches
steps.watchOut: leaving this acid-and-salt mix for hours on its own, which turns the meat chalky; move on to step 3 straight away.

steps.title: Second marinade
steps.text: Add 2 tbsp (30 g) thick curd, 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste, a pinch of turmeric, ¼ tsp cumin powder, ¼ tsp garam masala, ¼ tsp crushed kasuri methi and ½ tsp of the mustard/vegetable oil. Mix well.
steps.visualCue: thick orange-red coating that clings to the chicken and doesn't drip
steps.videoShot: curd and spices folded through the chicken
steps.watchOut: watery curd, which makes a runny coating and stops charring; hang the curd in a sieve or cloth for 15 min first if it looks thin.

steps.title: Cut the tikka vegetables
steps.text: Separate 25 g onion (¼ small) into single-layer petals and cut 25 g capsicum into 2–3 cm squares.
steps.visualCue: flat onion petals and capsicum squares that will lie flat on a tawa
steps.cameraCheck: onion petals and capsicum squares on the board
steps.videoShot: onion quarter pulled apart into petals
steps.watchOut: thin slivers, which burn to black bits; keep petals two layers thick.

steps.title: Add vegetables to the marinade
steps.text: Toss the onion and capsicum through the marinade on top of the chicken.
steps.visualCue: vegetables lightly coated in orange
steps.watchOut: over-mixing, which breaks the petals apart; fold gently.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and refrigerate.
steps.visualCue: covered bowl in the fridge; the coating turns a deeper red
steps.videoShot: bowl placed on the fridge shelf
steps.watchOut: leaving it uncovered, which dries the coating and picks up fridge smells; use a lid or cling film. Keep raw chicken on the lowest shelf.

steps.title: Chop the masala onion
steps.text: Finely chop 60 g (1 small) onion.
steps.visualCue: small, even pieces about 3–4 mm. Fine chopping matters because the gravy is not blended
steps.watchOut: big chunks, which stay raw-tasting and make the gravy lumpy; chop them smaller now, not later.

steps.title: Prepare the tomato
steps.text: Grate 120 g (1½ medium) tomato on a box grater, skin side out, and throw away the skin (or chop very finely). Slit 1 green chilli.
steps.visualCue: bowl of pulpy red tomato; the skin left flat in your hand
steps.cameraCheck: bowl of grated tomato and the slit chilli
steps.watchOut: grating your fingertips as the tomato gets small; stop with a thumb-sized piece left and chop that.

steps.title: Set out the masala spices
steps.text: On a plate, put ¼ tsp cumin seeds, ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, ½ tsp coriander powder, a pinch of cumin powder, a small pinch of turmeric, a big pinch of salt, ¼ tsp garam masala and ½ tsp kasuri methi, each in its own heap.
steps.visualCue: neat separate heaps
steps.watchOut: measuring spices over the hot pan, where steam clumps them and you miss the timing; have them ready beforehand.

steps.title: Skewer the tikka (optional)
steps.text: Thread chicken, onion and capsicum alternately onto 2 skewers. Without skewers, keep the pieces loose.
steps.visualCue: pieces touching lightly, not crushed together
steps.videoShot: chicken, onion, capsicum slid on in turn
steps.watchOut: packing pieces tight, which steams them instead of charring; leave a finger-width gap. Bamboo skewers that were not soaked burn.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron or heavy tawa on high and brush with the remaining ½ tsp oil.
steps.tip: using the oven or air fryer instead? See Equipment for the timings and skip to step 15 when it's done.
steps.visualCue: the oil shimmers and a drop of water flicked on sizzles off at once
steps.videoShot: oil brushed across the smoking-hot tawa
steps.watchOut: a lukewarm tawa, which makes the marinade stick and tear; wait for the sizzle test. Thick smoke means it is too hot, so lower the flame for a moment.

steps.title: Char the first side
steps.text: Lay the skewers (or pieces) flat on the tawa and leave them on medium-high without moving.
steps.visualCue: underside deep orange with black-edged spots; pieces release easily
steps.cameraCheck: one skewer lifted to show the char
steps.videoShot: skewer turned to reveal blackened edges
steps.watchOut: moving or prodding the chicken early, which tears the coating; if a piece sticks, wait another 30 sec and it will lift on its own.

steps.title: Char the other sides
steps.text: Turn and cook 2–3 more sides the same way.
steps.tip: it cooks a little more in the gravy, so stop as soon as there's no pink.
steps.visualCue: charred all over; when you cut the thickest piece the inside is white with no pink
steps.videoShot: knife cutting a charred tikka in half
steps.watchOut: pale grey chicken (too low a heat, so it is steaming; raise the heat) or black bitter patches covering the whole piece (too long; take it off).

steps.title: Flame-kiss (optional)
steps.text: Hold each skewer 3–4 cm over a high gas flame, turning it, for extra smoky edges.
steps.visualCue: a few extra blackened edges; smells smoky
steps.videoShot: tikka turning over a blue flame
steps.watchOut: dripping marinade flaring up, or the flame touching the chicken for long; keep it moving and the pieces a hand's width above the burner.

steps.title: Rest the tikka
steps.text: Slide the chicken and vegetables off the skewers onto a plate and scrape any browned bits from the tawa onto the plate.
steps.visualCue: charred orange tikka with blistered onion and capsicum
steps.videoShot: tikka pushed off the skewer with a fork
steps.watchOut: throwing away the browned bits on the tawa, which hold flavour; scrape them onto the plate.

steps.title: Heat fat for the masala
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat and add 1 tsp oil and 1 tsp (5 g) butter.
steps.visualCue: the butter melts and foams
steps.watchOut: high heat, which browns the butter (brown specks, burnt smell) before the cumin goes in; stay on medium.

steps.title: Temper cumin
steps.text: Add ¼ tsp cumin seeds.
steps.visualCue: seeds sizzle and turn a shade darker; nutty smell
steps.watchOut: seeds turning black and smelling acrid in seconds; if they do, wipe out the fat and start again.

steps.title: Brown the onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and the slit green chilli. Stir every 30 sec on medium.
steps.visualCue: onions evenly golden brown (not just translucent) and sweet-smelling. This is the base of tikka masala and the main difference from butter chicken
steps.watchOut: dark brown edges with a bitter smell (heat too high). Add 1 tbsp water and scrape the pan to rescue it. Pale, watery onion gives a raw-tasting gravy, so keep going.

steps.title: Add ginger-garlic paste
steps.text: Add ½ tsp ginger-garlic paste and stir.
steps.visualCue: the raw garlic smell is gone and the paste looks lightly golden
steps.watchOut: garlic that catches and browns fast, which tastes bitter; stir constantly and move to step 20 as soon as the raw smell goes.

steps.title: Add ground spices
steps.text: Lower the heat. Add the Kashmiri chilli powder, coriander powder, pinch of cumin powder and turmeric. Stir.
steps.visualCue: fat turns red; toasty smell
steps.watchOut: spices scorching (dark, sharp smell). Splash in 1 tbsp water at once and go straight to step 21. Have the tomato ready.

steps.title: Add tomato and salt
steps.text: Add the grated tomato and a big pinch of salt. Stir.
steps.visualCue: sizzles and loosens into a red mixture
steps.watchOut: tomato spitting; stand back a little and stir. Too little salt now makes the finished curry flat, so add the full pinch.

steps.title: Cook the masala down
steps.text: Cook on medium-low, stirring every minute, mashing with the spatula.
steps.visualCue: thick, jammy masala that leaves the sides of the pan, with oil shining at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: the edge of the masala showing separated oil
steps.videoShot: spatula drawing a line through thick masala
steps.watchOut: stopping early, when the masala is still wet and sour-smelling with no oil on top; keep cooking. If it sticks, add 1 tbsp water.

steps.title: Loosen
steps.text: Add 80 ml (⅓ cup) water, stir and bring to a simmer.
steps.visualCue: a thick, pourable gravy that coats the spoon
steps.cameraCheck: the back of a coated spoon
steps.videoShot: gravy dripping off the spoon slowly
steps.watchOut: a watery gravy that runs off the spoon; simmer 1–2 min more. If too thick, add water 1 tbsp at a time.

steps.title: Add the tikka
steps.text: Add the charred chicken, onion, capsicum and any plate juices. Fold in gently.
steps.visualCue: every piece coated in gravy
steps.watchOut: stirring hard, which breaks the charred coating off the chicken; fold with the back of the spoon.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Cover and simmer on low.
steps.visualCue: lazy bubbles; gravy clings to the chicken
steps.cameraCheck: the kadai with the lid lifted
steps.videoShot: steam rising as the lid comes off
steps.watchOut: a hard boil, which toughens the chicken and splits the gravy; lower the heat if bubbles are fast. Add 1–2 tbsp water if it gets too thick.

steps.title: Add kasuri methi
steps.text: Crush ½ tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan and stir.
steps.visualCue: a sharp "dhaba" aroma
steps.watchOut: adding too much, which turns the curry bitter; stay at ½ tsp.

steps.title: Add garam masala
steps.text: Sprinkle ¼ tsp garam masala and stir.
steps.visualCue: evenly mixed; a warm spice smell lifts off the pan
steps.watchOut: cooking it for long, which dulls the aroma; stir it in and move straight on.

steps.title: Finish with cream
steps.text: Turn the heat off and stir in 1 tbsp (15 ml) fresh cream.
steps.visualCue: the gravy turns a deeper orange-red with streaks of cream, still darker and redder than butter chicken
steps.watchOut: cream added on a hot flame, which splits into white specks. If it does, whisk in 1 tbsp warm water off the heat.

steps.title: Smoke it (optional)
steps.text: Place a red-hot coal in a steel katori in the middle of the curry, add a few drops of ghee or oil, and cover tightly.
steps.visualCue: smoke trapped under the lid; smoky smell when you open it
steps.videoShot: ghee dripped onto glowing coal, lid closed
steps.watchOut: leaving it more than 2–3 min, which makes the curry taste of ash; lift the katori out with tongs and open the lid away from your face.

steps.title: Garnish and plate
steps.text: Spoon into a bowl and top with 1 tbsp chopped coriander.
steps.visualCue: thick orange-red curry with charred chicken, onion and green capsicum showing
steps.watchOut: chopping the coriander early and leaving it out, when it wilts and darkens; chop it just before serving.

reasons: The home version is high in protein (~35 g). The chicken is charred on a tawa or grill with ½ tsp oil instead of fried, and total added fat is moderate (2 tsp oil, 1 tsp butter, 1 tbsp cream). There's no sugar or cashew, and onion, tomato and capsicum add vegetables and fibre. Saturated fat (about 41% of the limit) and sodium (about 53%) are the weak spots. Restaurant versions usually use more oil, butter and cream, often add cashew paste, sugar and sometimes food colour, and are saltier. They tend to be a little less rich than restaurant butter chicken, hence 5 rather than 4 (est.).

researchRating.basis: one of the world's best-known curries, a staple of Indian restaurant menus in Mumbai and the UK, with consistently high home-recipe scores (about 4.5 to 5 where vote counts are large). It scores a little below butter chicken because some people find restaurant versions generic or too heavy, and it is often called an Anglo-Indian creation rather than "authentic" Indian food. Some recipe ratings are lower (3 to 4.1, mostly from small samples).

storage: Fridge-safe in an airtight container for up to 2 days (cool it within 1 hour of cooking). Freezer: up to 1 month (est.); the capsicum softens and the cream may separate slightly, which comes back when you stir it while reheating. Reheating: on the stove on low with 2–3 tbsp water, stirring, until steaming hot right through. In the microwave, use 1-minute bursts and stir in between. Reheat only once.
leftoverRemix: Chicken tikka masala frankie (Mumbai-style roll). Shred the chicken and cook it down with the gravy until almost dry. Spread on a roti or paratha brushed with a beaten egg, add sliced onion, a squeeze of lemon, chaat masala and green chutney, then roll it up and toast seam-side down on a tawa.
burnOff: about 6.5 km of running (at ~70 kcal/km), or about 9 km of brisk walking (at ~50 kcal/km, est.).

navratri.reason: chicken, onion and garlic are all avoided in vrat

ekadashi.reason: chicken, onion and garlic are avoided (most common rule set assumed)

jain.reason: chicken, onion, garlic and fresh ginger (root rule, Patch 05)

ramadan.reason: use halal-sourced chicken; rich and fairly salty (about 50% of the 2,000 mg sodium limit), so better as the main iftar dish than as sehri

jain.reason: chicken, onion, garlic and fresh ginger (a root) are in the recipe

sattvik.reason: chicken is not sattvik, and the recipe uses onion and ginger-garlic paste

glutenFree.reason: chicken, curd, tomato, vegetables and whole or ground spices; no wheat, rava, maida or hing (check masala and chilli powder labels for fillers)

dairyFree.reason: curd 30 g, butter 5 g and cream 15 ml are dairy; use coconut yoghurt, oil and coconut cream (see Dairy-free variant)

variants.reason: the dish is defined by chicken, and the masala is built on browned onion and ginger-garlic; a Jain version would be a different dish.
the dish is defined by chicken (plus curd, butter and cream); a plant-based tikka masala is a different dish.
Main recipe already gluten-free (no wheat, rava, maida or hing).
replacing the chicken gives Paneer Tikka Masala (paneer tikka in the same masala), which is a different dish (a Zomato Mumbai "Paneer Tikka Masala" dish page exists).
